meta.title: Message Queue Delivery Guarantees: At-Least-Once Means Duplicates

segments.label: Producer publishes once; broker persists it until it receives an ack
Consumer receives the message and charges the card — but crashes before it can ack
Ack never arrives, so at-least-once redelivers — the card gets charged twice

messages.label: OK: persisted, waiting for consumer ack

cards.title: Why 'At-Least-Once' Means Duplicates Are Possible
items: The broker's only guarantee is that the message gets delivered one or more times, never zero
It has no way to tell 'consumer crashed before processing' apart from 'consumer crashed right after processing but before acking'
So on any doubt — an ack timeout, a dropped connection — it resends

cards.title: The Three Delivery Guarantees
items: At-most-once: send and forget — a message can be lost, but is never duplicated
At-least-once: retry until acked — a message can be duplicated, but is never lost
Exactly-once (end-to-end) isn't a transport-level guarantee — it's at-least-once plus an idempotent consumer or dedup layer on top

cards.title: How to Make the Consumer Safe
items: Track processed message IDs in a dedup table or cache with a TTL, and skip anything already seen
Make the side effect itself idempotent — 'set status = charged' instead of 'charge again'
Where the broker supports it, use its native exactly-once feature (Kafka transactions, SQS FIFO with a deduplication ID)
